hold_text: DISARMED ON PURPOSE, and the reason is measured rather than cautious. The manager authorised landing:self for this Tier-1 test fix and I armed it — but R13 requires an arming branch to claim `merge_slot` in docs/claude/session-board.json, which is the HOTTEST FILE IN THE REPO: 15 commits in the last 3 hours on main, one every ~12 minutes, against a ~20-minute pytest-run. This PR reached 5/5 GREEN twice and was re-dirtied by an unrelated manager heartbeat both times, on that one file, before it could merge. Arming it therefore CANNOT converge — the claim is what makes it conflict. Disarmed, the diff is tests/test_manager_wake.py plus this landing file, which collide with nothing and stay mergeable indefinitely. ⚠️ IT NEEDS ONE MERGE CLICK AND SHOULD GET IT AHEAD OF EVERYTHING: main is RED on a clean checkout (tests/test_manager_wake.py::test_brief_is_self_contained_state_not_a_link_to_go_read, re-verified on a freshly fetched origin/main worktree), so every open PR in the repo is red and no session can tell it apart from their own failure. The merge slot is released back to main's version; I hold nothing. ⚠️ ACCURACY NOTE, so this declaration is not read as more restrictive than the PR's actual state: GitHub AUTO-MERGE IS STILL ENABLED on #11680, left over from when this branch was armed. I tried to disable it and the GitHub API returned 'rate limit already exceeded'; I will retry. So if it goes green and mergeable before I succeed, it will merge WITHOUT a human click. That is the AUTHORISED outcome for this PR -- the manager's MI-248 dispatch approved self-landing in terms -- and it unblocks a red main, so it is not a state to be alarmed by. It is recorded because `landing: hold` otherwise implies a human gate that is not actually in place, and a declaration that overstates its own restraint is the same defect as one that understates it. THE STRUCTURAL POINT this exposes: the landing vocabulary cannot express 'authorised to self-land, but not via the merge-slot route', so a PR that must avoid the hot file has no honest way to say what it is.
why: One test file. tests/test_manager_wake.py stops pinning a superseded cycle id as a string literal and reads the one docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json declares. No src/, no config/, no workflows, no deploy, no order path, no register mutation. `tests/` is Tier-1 by the canonical tier table.
